summary: @servicetitan/cp-mfe-dev preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` script that runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases, unzips it into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunBinary, [math_init.js])` against a sibling file shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a 728KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob whose contents are a shuffled multi-thousand-entry string/opcode array permuted at runtime by a rotation function (`WV8StW`) — heavy dictionary/opcode obfuscation that is only meaningful when executed by the downloaded Bun binary and is opaque to Node-based inspection. Handing an obfuscated blob to a second language runtime at install time is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern; the package's advertised purpose (a ServiceTitan MFE dev helper library) has no functional need for a second runtime. The package name `@servicetitan/cp-mfe-dev` mimics ServiceTitan's private npm scope and its peerDependencies list additional `@servicetitan/*` packages, making the artifact usable as a dependency-confusion lure targeting organizations with an internal ServiceTitan scope. The shipped `dist/` files are a thin SDK-shaped stub that serves as cover for the install-time dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
